title: Shell following trusts the line's exit status rather than the cd's (`cd /abs || true`, `cd /abs; cmd` re-follow at /abs after a failed cd)
outcome: engram_settle_shell_move anchors a pending move (the line's single leading literal cd) when the whole command succeeds. With `cd /abs || true`, or `cd /abs; cmd` where cmd succeeds, a failed cd still ends in a successful line. TermAl then presumes the shell at /abs, though it stayed where it was. Later commands can be credited or bounded in the wrong place, and overlap may be under-marked. This predates PI-26a, and the old code behaved the same.
acceptance: TermAl follows a leading cd only when its success is implied by the line's success (the cd is the line's only command, or is joined to the rest by `&&` all the way), and loses the shell between both places otherwise; a test covers `cd /abs || true` and `cd /abs; true`
